title: New player guide - House of Pips Wiki
description: Your first hour of House of Pips: Nana's tutorial, the main menu, your first match and what to unlock first.
html:
New player guide

1. Take Nana's tutorial #

A brand-new career starts with most of the main menu locked: Play, Puzzles and Multiplayer all say "Finish Nana's tutorial first."

Open Tutorials and play Nana's tutorial. In a few minutes she teaches the whole table, from pips and the hammer to scoring, the boneyard and winning a hand.

Finishing it unlocks the rest of the menu and the Old School mode, and Nana invites you straight into a short Old School game against her (first to 75). See Tutorials for both tutorials.

2. Find your way around the menu #

  • Play starts a match in the mode shown on the button. A new career plays Classic Table, first to 150.
  • Puzzles are hand-made solo challenges. See Puzzles.
  • Multiplayer plays a friend or a stranger through Steam. See Online play.
  • Tutorials replays Nana's lesson and opens Rival School.
  • Modes chooses which ruleset Play uses. See Game modes.
  • Perks is the compendium where you unlock perks for your drafts with Bone Bucks.
  • Skill tree spends the skill points you earn by levelling up.
  • Slap Track pays one reward for every career level.
  • Career shows your records and match history.
  • Supply Shop, Inventory, Cosmetics and Choose your avatar hold the things you buy and earn. See Shop, Bone Boxes and cosmetics.
  • Settings has sound, display, language, accessibility and voice chat options. See Settings and accessibility.

3. Play your first match #

A match is a race to the target score, played over several hands:

  1. You and Rival each draw a face-down bone for the hammer. The higher double wins it, and the hammer plays first.
  2. You choose your opening perk from a draft of cards, then Rival does the same.
  3. Each hand you pick your seven bones face-down from the shuffled set, then take turns playing them onto the table.
  4. Whenever the open ends add up to a multiple of five after your play, you score that total.
  5. The hand ends when someone plays their last bone, or when nobody can play. The winner also scores the loser's remaining pips.
  6. The loser of each hand drafts another perk, and the next hand begins.

Matches, hands and drafts explains every step, and Domino rules covers the dominoes themselves.

4. What to do with your first Bone Bucks #

Every hand pays Bone Bucks, win or lose. Good first purchases:

  • Unlock perks in the Perks compendium. Your drafts only offer perks you have unlocked, and you start with just three: Double Trouble, Zero Hero and Hot Streak. Unlocking 5 perks of one rarity opens the next rarity for purchase.
  • Spend skill points as you level. End Count and Reader's Eye on the Table Sense tab make the table much easier to read.
  • Try a supply such as a Table Pass from the Supply Shop.

5. Keep learning #

  • Hover any perk, button or bone for a tooltip.
  • Open the Ledger during a match to see exactly how every score was made.
  • Rival School (in Tutorials) teaches seven table styles through short lessons.
  • The FAQ and troubleshooting answers the questions new players ask most.
